title: Governor Pritzker's tax record questioned by House Republicans
text:
← Back to the wire
Governor Pritzker’s tax record questioned by House Republicans
Governor JB Pritzker's record on taxation is under scrutiny as critics cite increased burdens for Illinois families since he took office. The debate centers around reported rises in various state levies and alternative proposals from House Republicans.
Governor JB Pritzker’s claims of delivering tax cuts to working families were challenged on Oct. 15, with critics saying Illinois families have faced higher taxes and rising costs during his administration.
According to the Caucus Blog, working families have seen an $85.6 billion increase in their tax burden under Pritzker, resulting from 63 tax and fee hikes that impact both individuals and businesses. In the most recent fiscal year, Illinois residents reportedly paid $15.2 billion more in taxes than they would have before Pritzker took office.
The article states that Illinois now ranks first in several categories: highest property taxes, highest combined state and local taxes, and highest cell phone taxes. Citing a WalletHub study, it notes that "Illinoisans face the highest tax rates in the nation," with a median-household model showing a tax burden 53% above the national average.
The criticism extends to budget management as well. The Governor is accused of balancing so-called "balanced budgets" by relying on taxpayers: "Just this year, he signed the largest budget in state history, relying on approximately $800 million in new taxes and revenue measures," the blog argues this approach fails to provide relief for residents.
House Republicans say they have proposed alternatives focused on reducing government spending and offering meaningful tax relief. This includes HB 9, which aims to lower property taxes, and HB 5738, intended to temporarily suspend the state sales tax on gasoline.
